contracts.assertions: JS `Socket.onclose` runs `_clearAcks()` on every close, so a transport drop that the manager retries settles a pending acknowledgement exactly as `disconnect()` does: `socket.timeout(N).emit` and a configured-`ackTimeout` callback receive the disconnect error and the registry is left empty (JS asserts `Object.keys(socket.acks).length === 0`), the `emitWithAck` continuation is resumed with `.disconnected` as JS rejects the promise, and a callback registered without `withError` is removed silently without being invoked. The real server-side transport kill covers the same contract end to end with an emit the server never acknowledges. The promise variant (JS-104) is certified by its own async tests: `emitWithAck` throws `.disconnected` both on an explicit disconnect and on a retried transport drop.

`_clearAcks` skips an acknowledgement whose packet is still in `sendBuffer`: the packet has not reached the server, so it goes out on the next CONNECT and the acknowledgement is still owed. The throttled-timer scenario is what buffers a packet while the socket still believes it is connected (JS sets `_pingTimeoutTime` into the past; here `hasPingExpired`), and the buffered emit is answered after the reconnect.

`_clearAcks` retires the per-attempt acknowledgement `_drainQueue` registered, and the callback `_addToQueue` appended decides what the close means for the entry: with retries left it keeps its place in `_queue` with `pending = false` and `onconnect`'s `_drainQueue(true)` re-sends it under a fresh id; once `tryCount > retries` the entry is discarded and the user's acknowledgement settles with the error. The queue never drains while the socket is disconnected.

Real /abc handshake receives exact query key &a and value &=?a without URL delimiter corruption; asserts decoded value equals original. Native connectParams replaces JS query object.

Original retry budget one and emits echo 1,2,3 before connect: immediate queue lengths 1,2,3; ACK-time lengths 2,1,0; final nil error and integer 3; complete ordered ACK values. Real engine packet-create recorder additionally asserts CONNECT, ACK IDs 0/1/2 with exact echo payloads, then DISCONNECT. Native positive deadline scaled to two seconds; only explicit root CONNECT/DISCONNECT namespace is canonicalized.

Encode message=test through the real polling packet encoder, assert exact 4test frame and POST body, decode and assert exactly one text delivery test with no error. Native client dispatch replaces returned JS packet object; no hand-constructed type-prefix expression substitutes for the encoder.

For each original malformed single packet (empty string and a123), require exactly parser error, no text delivery and closed engine. Native engine error callback replaces JS error packet {type:error,data:parser error}; closure is an additional transport assertion.

Decode each original malformed payload ({, {}, ["a123", "a456"]) through parsePollingMessage, assert exact single parser error, transport-error close and no deliveries. Also verify the empty payload edge case from decodePayload implementation, explicitly additional to the three original inputs.

Original [1,2,3,4] binary bytes encoded with the production createBinaryDataForSend protocol implementation in WebSocket mode return raw Data without prefix; decode as binary and assert exactly those bytes. Foundation.Data replaces Buffer; callbacks replace returned packet object.

Original binary bytes [1,2,3,4] encoded through the production binary encoder in polling mode produce exactly bAQIDBA==; decoding dispatches the exact original Data. Native Data replaces Buffer and binary callback replaces returned message packet.

Decode exact [1,2,3,4] binary input as Data; assert byte equality and no text delivery. Foundation.Data is the native binary representation corresponding to both ArrayBuffer input and output; no JS type constructor is required.

Encode text test and binary [1,2,3,4] through real sendPollMessage and actual POST joiner: exact 4test record-separator bAQIDBA==. Decode payload, assert exact text and binary values and combined delivery sequence text then binary. Separate per-type arrays alone are not accepted as order proof.

Request original getbin before connect on forced-base64 polling; assert b64=1 transport negotiation and received bytes re-encode exactly as YXNkZmFzZGY=. Native Data replaces the legacy JS {base64:true,data:...} wrapper used when ArrayBuffer/Blob are unavailable. The transferable binary content and base64 transport are tested; Swift does not emulate absence of native binary storage.

On namespace /no, emit original reserved disconnecting event with goodbye; assert exactly one synchronous error containing the exact quoted name and reserved-event message, plus no buffered packet. Native nonthrowing emit reports through error event rather than a JS throw; rejection and diagnostic are preserved.

All eleven original invalid JSON/payload inputs must throw native invalidDataArray; original five invalid attachment headers must throw invalidPacket; 999 string must throw invalidPacketType. Native typed errors replace the corresponding JS error-message categories. Passing integer 999 to parseString is statically unrepresentable (String required; Data has a separate entry point), not a silently accepted input.

Check original valid CONNECT without payload (type connect, namespace root, empty native data), then every original invalid payload shape: scalar/array CONNECT, payload-bearing DISCONNECT, scalar/object EVENT, object pretending toString, boolean/null event names and reserved names. Original packet objects are represented as their wire headers plus unchanged JSON payloads; native throwing decoder is the validity boundary instead of a standalone Boolean helper.

Real default Engine.IO connection opens; close then immediately send hi, await close and local refused-write completion, observe 200 ms with no incoming application packet. Require empty outgoing queue and no 4hi in actual server POST bodies or WebSocket frames. Native absence of queued/wire packet replaces JS packetCreate negative event assertion.

Real polling server maxPayload 100: send original a*99, b*30, c*30, d*35, euro*33 and f*99, require all six exact echoed messages in order. Assert multiple POST batches and every observed body at most 100 UTF-8 bytes. This is raw Engine.IO, not a substitute Socket.IO envelope test.

Real polling maxPayload 100: send a*101 followed immediately by b, require transport-error closure with HTTP 413 for the rejected first write. Oversized first packet is sent rather than silently dropped or preventing error completion. Native typed close detail replaces JS close event.

Inject bad data through the manager engine-data entry point on a real connection. Assert parse-error disconnect, reconnect signal before reconnection, new engine object, retired engine closed, and different namespace SID. Listener setup uses the native namespace connect callback; the original engine identity and closed-state assertions are explicit.

Successful candidate probe with outstanding polling GET; request deferred close, then fail the active polling transport using the engine error entry point. Assert upgradeError before close, transport-error close exactly once, candidate aborted, queue empty, and no duplicate callbacks from late candidate failure. This follows the original active-transport failure rather than substituting a candidate-only fallback.

Assert hasPingExpired=false before open and immediately after. Use controlled monotonic clock to expire deadline; three successive reads return true with no synchronous close, then exactly one deferred ping timeout close. Additional ping-reset checks retain the original repeated-expiry and close-reason assertions.

Original localhost, /engine.io, timestampRequests=true, timestampParam=t. Assert http scheme, host, default port omission, exact no-trailing-slash path, one nonempty t value matching original [0-9A-Za-z_-]+ alphabet. Original localhost, /engine.io, timestampRequests=true, timestampParam=woot. Assert ws scheme, host, default port omission, exact no-trailing-slash path, one nonempty woot value matching original alphabet. Native required transport/EIO query fields are retained; query ordering is normalized.

Pass the complete original custom-header and explicit Cookie dictionary. Assert engine retains the exact value dictionary and the real WebSocket upgrade request contains every original header/value unchanged. Swift dictionary value equality replaces JS object identity; public upstream fixture strings are not credentials.

The JS internal randomString helper promises eight characters and different consecutive values. Swift does not expose that helper or its exact length; wire cache-busting uses a separate native contract, not a fabricated compatible helper.

Real polling-only connection with withCredentials=true. Fixture sets original cookies 1=1 and 2=2; after open, a raw message is echoed and the server-observed POST Cookie contains exactly both name/value pairs. Cookie pair order is normalized because Foundation owns serialization order; no missing or additional cookie is accepted. Original ten-millisecond sleep is replaced by the completed-open/cookie-processing barrier.

Real polling-only connection with withCredentials=false. Fixture sets original cookies 1=1 and 2=2; send on open, await echo and assert the subsequent server-observed POST has no Cookie header. Native nil corresponds to JS undefined.

Parse original foo=bar Set-Cookie input with Foundation; assert name foo and value bar. Native HTTPCookie replaces the Node object while preserving every field asserted by this simple original scenario.

The Node cookie parser returns only name/value/expires and overwrites expiry in header iteration order. Foundation preserves domain/path/security and owns native expiration policy. The conflicting Max-Age/Expires sample is not declared object-for-object equivalent; native parsing and security scope have separate tests.

Parse original foo=bar=bar&foo=foo&John=Doe&Doe=John; Domain=.example.com; Path=/; HttpOnly; Secure. Assert name foo and the complete original value including embedded equals and ampersands. HTTPCookie is the native object representation.

The standalone JS parseuri helper exposes a parsed-component object and handles a corpus of shorthand inputs. Swift uses Foundation URL/URLComponents instead; no identical public parseuri result or input grammar is promised. Absolute transport URL validation remains separately tested.

JS can be configured with transports: [] and reports No transports available. Swift has fixed native transports and rejects contradictory forcePolling/forceWebsockets options; the empty transport-list API is not representable. A fail-before-network native configuration test remains.

Real a*101 exceeds 100-byte polling server limit. Error callback must carry SocketTransportError with HTTP 413, operation write, polling write (HTTP 413) description and empty body; close must follow the error with transport error and identical detail object. Native URLSession completed response/type replaces XHR readyState/TransportError fields; queued b additionally covers JS-151.

Real WebSocket a*101 over 100-byte server limit closes with transport close, typed detail operation close, code 1009, empty close reason and websocket close (WebSocket 1009) description. Require no preceding error callback. Native SocketTransportError fields replace CloseEvent fields; IE11 branch is platform-specific.

Real polling request with nonexistent SID returns 400: error callback asserts typed polling read error, exact status and exact Session ID unknown JSON body; close follows with transport error and same detail. Stale request injected at transport layer because user query may not override engine-owned SID. Native completed URLSession response replaces XHR readyState.

Real WebSocket handshake carrying nonexistent SID must report typed websocket close-operation error with native underlying error; close follows with transport error and the same detail object. Native URLSession error replaces JS generic error Event; no unsupported HTTP response-body/status claim is made.
